explanation: The N88S mutation reduces indinavir binding through an indirect allosteric mechanism rather than direct ligand contact. Asn88's polar side chain and larger volume contribute to maintaining the precise geometry of the C-terminal dimer interface; replacement with the smaller, less polar serine diminishes the structural scaffold supporting the active site architecture, likely destabilizing the protease conformation optimized for indinavir recognition. The 7.3 Å minimum distance to the ligand, combined with the mutation's location in the dimer-stabilizing region, suggests resistance arises from compromised active site geometry or reduced conformational stability rather than steric clash or direct interaction loss, effectively lowering the affinity of the protease for the inhibitor.
